headline: KSE-100 sheds 2,541 points to 167,971 as Hormuz escalation and a near-5% 10Y rattle sentiment; Tuesday's record $21.4bn SBP reserves spark an early rebound ahead of Wednesday's FOMC verdict
mood: Hawkish crosscurrents · Hormuz risk premium the swing factor into FOMC

five_things.html: The KSE-100 shed 2,541.20 points (−1.49%) on Monday to close at 167,970.66, its worst session in weeks, as fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iranian attacks on Gulf shipping triggered broad de-risking. Breadth was ugly — just 83 of 492 traded names advanced against 373 decliners — while volume thinned to 570.5m shares from 687.5m the prior session. Business Recorder and The Nation confirm the print.

Buying returned at the open Tuesday, with the index up 1,999.58 points (+1.19%) to 169,970.23 by 9:35am as the State Bank's FX reserves hit an all-time high of $21.4bn on Eurobond inflows. Index-heavy names — OGDC, PPL, MARI, POL, MCB, MEBL, HBL and NBP — led, with autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs, power and refinery all in the green per Business Recorder.

The US 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5% intraday for the first time since 2023 before settling near 4.99%, while the 2-year climbed to 4.66%, its highest since mid-2024. Wall Street slipped in response — S&P 500 −0.48% to 7,619.98, Dow −0.29%, Nasdaq −0.56% — with forecasters split ahead of Wednesday's decision: J.P. Morgan sees a 25bp hike while Goldman Sachs calls one "very unlikely." CNBC and FedRateCalc.

Brent settled at $108.15/bbl, a four-month high, and WTI at $102.64, both up over 2%, after Oman postponed Gulf-Iran talks on Strait of Hormuz shipping and Saudi Arabia's drone-damaged East-West pipeline stayed shut. Vessel transits through the Strait fell to single digits over the weekend, reviving the crude risk premium per Vantage Markets and Trading Economics. A costlier import bill is a direct headwind for Pakistan's external account.

Gold eased roughly 1% to $4,310/oz and silver slid to about $63.30, both retreating from richer levels as a firmer dollar and near-90% odds of a Wednesday rate move pressured the complex — silver's industrial linkage leaves it more exposed than gold's safe-haven bid. Per Kitco and Yahoo Finance.

matrix.local_html: Monday's 1.49% PSX rout — driven by renewed Houthi and Iranian attacks in the Gulf — gave way to a firmer Tuesday open as the State Bank's reserves hit a record $21.4bn on Eurobond proceeds. The SBP has held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting even as August CPI ran hot at 11.15% y/y, well above the 5–7% target band, per Trading Economics. Six-month KIBOR sits at 11.86%. The IMF's fourth EFF review mission lands September 23 for a near two-week visit, with roughly $1bn in tranche disbursement riding on progress against fiscal targets that have slipped on wheat and sugar market interventions. Meanwhile the Finance Bill 2026 tax overhaul — salaried-slab relief, a 1.25% minimum tax, and digital-invoicing enforcement — continues to work through implementation.
matrix.gcc_html: The Hormuz stand-off is the region's dominant swing factor: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after drone strikes, and Oman's postponement of Gulf-Iran talks has pushed Brent to a four-month high near $108. Against that backdrop, OPEC+ continues its gradual output normalisation, having added 188,000 bpd in August across seven members. Non-oil momentum stays intact — the bloc's composite PMI held at 51.5 for a 21st straight month above the 50 mark, with UAE's reading climbing to 54.2 and Saudi Arabia's at 56.6. Riyadh's PIF Board approved its 2026-2030 strategy, pivoting from giga-project scale toward commercial returns in logistics, mining and AI infrastructure ahead of the Saudi Mega Projects Summit (Sep 28-30), which will showcase a pipeline exceeding $200bn.
matrix.global_html: US markets softened Monday as the 10-year Treasury yield briefly breached 5% for the first time since 2023, AI-IPO safety jitters weighed on chipmakers, and crude's Hormuz-driven spike added to inflation angst. The Fed's Wednesday decision is now the week's pivot: consensus is split between a 25bp hike (J.P. Morgan) and a hold (Goldman Sachs) — a rare divergence this close to a meeting. On the policy front, Congress returned from recess with government funding secured through December 11 but no consensus on an AI regulatory framework, leaving the field to a 29-state patchwork with only four legislative days left before members turn to the November 3 midterms.

legislative.policy_html: IMF's 4th EFF/3rd RSF review mission arrives Sep 23, alongside the Finance Bill 2026 tax overhaul
legislative.sectors: Banks, FMCG, Real Estate, Sovereign Eurobonds
legislative.impact_html: Wins: salaried taxpayers, property transactors, and banks positioned for the ~$1bn EFF tranche Loses: importers facing a wider bill from the Hormuz oil shock; fiscal credibility dented by wheat/sugar intervention slippage

legislative.policy_html: PIF's 2026-2030 strategy re-weights toward commercial returns, alongside continued OPEC+ output normalisation
legislative.impact_html: Wins: logistics, mining and AI-infrastructure allocations; oil exporters capturing the Hormuz risk premium Loses: giga-project contractors facing write-downs and stretched delivery timelines

legislative.policy_html: Congress returns without an AI framework, funded through Dec 11, as the Fed's Sep 16 decision looms
legislative.impact_html: Wins: AI incumbents facing no near-term federal guardrails Loses: rate-sensitive growth stocks and long-duration bonds if the Fed leans hawkish

desk_stance_html: We read Tuesday's early bounce as relief buying against a still-hawkish macro backdrop, not a trend reversal. The Hormuz risk premium in oil is a direct tax on Pakistan's import bill and a headwind for the current account even as SBP reserves hit a record $21.4bn. Wednesday's FOMC decision — genuinely contested between a hike and a hold — is the week's key swing factor for global risk appetite and, by extension, foreign flows into frontier equities. We would fade strength into the 170,438 resistance band and treat a close below 167,442 as confirmation that Monday's selling has more room to run. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 sheds 2,541 points as Hormuz escalation meets a near-5% Treasury yield — but Tuesday's record FX reserves print is already clawing back the losses.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
Wall Street softened Monday: S&P 500 −0.48% to 7,619.98, Dow −0.29% to 52,421.20, Nasdaq −0.56% to 26,186.41. The real story was rates — the US 10-year briefly topped 5% intraday for the first time since 2023 before settling near 4.99%, while the 2-year climbed to 4.66%. Wednesday's FOMC decision is now a coin flip: J.P. Morgan expects a 25bp hike, Goldman Sachs calls one "very unlikely."

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 fell 1.49% (−2,541 pts) to 167,970.66 on Monday as fresh Houthi and Iranian attacks in the Gulf triggered broad de-risking — only 83 of 492 names advanced. Tuesday opened with relief buying, up nearly 2,000 points, after the State Bank's FX reserves hit an all-time high of $21.4bn on Eurobond inflows. SBP holds its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting despite August CPI at 11.15% y/y. The IMF's fourth EFF review mission lands September 23, with roughly $1bn in tranche disbursement at stake.

GCC
Brent settled at $108.15/bbl, a four-month high, and WTI at $102.64, after Oman postponed Gulf-Iran Hormuz talks and Saudi Arabia's drone-damaged East-West pipeline stayed shut. OPEC+ continues gradually restoring output even as the crisis lifts prices. Non-oil momentum holds — GCC composite PMI at 51.5, Saudi at 56.6, UAE at 54.2. Saudi's PIF approved its 2026-2030 strategy, pivoting from giga-project scale toward logistics, mining and AI infrastructure ahead of the September 28-30 Mega Projects Summit in Riyadh.

GLOBAL
Gold eased about 1% to $4,310/oz and silver slid to roughly $63.30 as rate-hike odds firmed and the dollar strengthened. In Washington, Congress returned from recess with funding secured through December 11 but no consensus on AI regulation, leaving a 29-state patchwork in place with just four legislative days left before the November 3 midterms.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: IMF's 4th EFF review (Sep 23) + Finance Bill 2026 tax reforms — wins for salaried taxpayers and banks; loses for importers facing a wider bill from the oil shock.
• GCC: PIF's 2026-2030 strategy + OPEC+ output normalisation — wins for logistics/mining/AI allocations; loses for giga-project contractors facing write-downs.
• Global: Congress punts on AI rules; FOMC decision Sep 16 — wins for AI incumbents facing no near-term guardrails; loses for rate-sensitive growth stocks if the Fed leans hawkish.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 167,442 (Monday's session low) · pivot 167,971 (Monday's close) · resistance 170,438 (Monday's intraday high). We'd fade strength into resistance and treat a close below support as confirmation Monday's selling has more room to run. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
